# Noah compatibility fixtures

`nitro-v0.0.144-crypto.json` is generated by
`cargo run --example nitro-vectors`. It repeats the exact pure-Rust formulas in
Nitro v0.0.144 lib.rs, independently of the new FFI implementations. It uses the
public BIP39 `abandon … about` vector, empty passphrase, Bitcoin signed-message
hash and libsecp256k1 RFC6979 signing. Never use this seed for real funds.
Indices 0, 1, 7, 2^31-1, 2^31 and 2^32-1 cover normal and hardened children.
Network only affects extended-key serialization, so all four SDK networks have
the same compressed public keys and DER signatures.

`noah-v2-schema42.sqlite` is an initialized, empty test wallet with known public
identity and server/mailbox keys. Reproduce with `cargo run --example
nitro-snapshot-fixture` after removing the fixture intentionally. Its schema is
generated by Bark bfbe6b7c. Comparing its migration sources against
`bark-0.7.1` (1d1e4c8950769ca3fd884088955e7a5316d39b1d), pinned by Nitro
v0.0.144, shows identical migration SQL; the sole difference is a height
conversion in a migration unit test. This proves the schema format used by
v2 plaintext `db.sqlite`; it is not an end-user backup archive. Host contracts
copy it before validating and check identity and unchanged source bytes.
